name: Colonel gray epaulet sleeve
size_basis: CAPR 39-1 Fig A5-1 / A5-6 give no inch size. Scale 178 px per inch from the 1 in oak leaf on the Major sleeve in Fig A5-1; trapezoid (350 px bottom, 306 px top, 684 px tall at that scale) and all feature positions measured on the figure. Officer sleeves come in two sizes (standard / smaller); the figure shows no measurable difference, so one size is built.
provenance: measured from CAPR 39-1 Fig A5-1 (gray) and A5-6 (blue); CAP lettering cleaned from traced glyphs; grade pieces are this family's own assets

dimensions.grade_bottom_note: DAFI 36-2903 7.1.5.1: 5/8 in from the end of the epaulet; figure shows 0.63-0.71 in

mounts.uniform: Class B blue shirt (long/short sleeve, men and women)
mounts.rule: slipped over the shirt epaulet; officers gray with embroidered grade, cadet officers blue with miniature metal grade (CAPR 39-1 4.1.6.1.1, 4.1.6.1.4). NCOs wear the 3 1/2 / 4 in chevron on the sleeve instead; cadet NCOs and Airmen wear metal collar chevrons (no sleeve).

mounts.uniform: Corporate aviator shirt (white), worn alone or under the blazer
mounts.rule: same gray / blue sleeve (4.2.5.1.1.1, 4.2.5.1.1.4). Individuals without grade wear gray sleeves with no insignia (1.2.x, 4.2.5).
no epaulet sleeves; grade insignia is optional on the black blazer nameplate (officers and NCOs), not allowed for cadets (4.2.3.1.1.2, 4.2.4.1.1.2).

orientation_note: Colonel eagle MIRRORED to follow the regulation text: beak toward the wearer's right shoulder = viewer's LEFT on a front view (CAPR 39-1 6.1.14.4.1; OCP/ABU grade rules). The figures (A5-1/A5-2) draw it toward the viewer's right. Decision 2026-10-13.
